description: Grapefruit inhibits metabolic enzymes, significantly increasing warfarin levels and raising the risk of severe internal bleeding.
recommendation: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice completely while on warfarin therapy.

food_display: Vitamin K Rich Foods (Spinach, Kale, Broccoli)
description: Vitamin K directly counteracts the anticoagulant effect of warfarin, decreasing its effectiveness and increasing clotting risk.
recommendation: Maintain a consistent, stable intake of green leafy vegetables rather than sudden large portions.

description: Acute alcohol consumption slows warfarin breakdown and increases bleeding risk, while chronic drinking decreases its efficacy.
recommendation: Avoid or strictly limit alcohol consumption while taking warfarin.

description: Grapefruit blocks the CYP3A4 enzyme, leading to dangerously elevated atorvastatin blood levels and higher risk of severe muscle damage (rhabdomyolysis) and liver toxicity.
recommendation: Avoid consuming large quantities of grapefruit juice (over 1.2 liters daily) or consult your doctor about switching to a statin unaffected by grapefruit.

description: Excessive alcohol consumption combined with rosuvastatin increases liver enzyme levels and potential risk of hepatic impairment.
recommendation: Limit alcohol intake while taking cholesterol-lowering statins.

description: Calcium in milk, curd, and fortified products binds directly to ciprofloxacin in the digestive tract, decreasing drug absorption by up to 40%.
recommendation: Do not take ciprofloxacin with dairy products alone. Take it at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after consuming milk or dairy.

description: Calcium forms insoluble chelates with tetracycline, preventing gut absorption and rendering the antibiotic largely ineffective.
recommendation: Take tetracycline on an empty stomach with a full glass of water, at least 1-2 hours before or after dairy foods.

description: Alcohol strongly potentiates the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism, significantly increasing the risk of life-threatening lactic acidosis and severe hypoglycemia.
recommendation: Avoid excessive acute or chronic alcohol consumption while taking metformin for diabetes.

food_display: Potassium-Rich Foods & Salt Substitutes (Bananas, Coconut Water)
description: ACE inhibitors reduce potassium excretion. High dietary potassium or potassium-based salt substitutes can cause dangerous hyperkalemia (high blood potassium).
recommendation: Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium chloride unless prescribed by your doctor.

description: ARBs like telmisartan increase potassium retention. Consuming high potassium foods or potassium salt substitutes may lead to irregular heart rhythms due to hyperkalemia.
recommendation: Discuss your dietary potassium intake and salt substitutes with your physician.

food_display: Soy Products (Soy Milk, Tofu, Soy Flour)
description: Soy compounds inhibit gastrointestinal absorption of levothyroxine, leading to uncontrolled hypothyroidism and requiring higher medicine doses.
recommendation: Separate the ingestion of levothyroxine and soy products by at least 4 hours.

description: Caffeine and coffee compounds bind levothyroxine in the gut, reducing thyroid hormone absorption by 25-50%.
recommendation: Take levothyroxine with plain water on an empty stomach at least 30-60 minutes before your morning coffee or breakfast.

description: Grapefruit can increase blood concentrations of amlodipine, potentially causing excessive blood pressure drops, peripheral edema, and lightheadedness.
recommendation: Limit or avoid grapefruit intake while taking amlodipine, and monitor for dizziness or flushing.

description: Metronidazole triggers an acute disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol: intense nausea, severe abdominal cramps, violent vomiting, facial flushing, and tachycardia.
recommendation: Do not consume any alcohol during metronidazole treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.

description: Combining aspirin with alcohol exacerbates mucosal irritation in the stomach, dramatically increasing the risk of gastric bleeding and peptic ulcers.
recommendation: Avoid drinking alcohol when taking aspirin regularly for pain or cardioprotection.

description: Alcohol and NSAIDs both irritate the stomach lining and impair renal blood flow, multiplying the risk of stomach ulcers, GI bleeding, and kidney strain.
recommendation: Avoid consuming alcohol while taking ibuprofen, especially on an empty stomach.

description: While not directly contraindicated, alcohol impairs the immune response and can worsen antibiotic side effects like dizziness and stomach upset.
recommendation: Avoid alcohol while fighting bacterial infections to support recovery and reduce GI discomfort.

description: Antacids containing aluminum or magnesium reduce the peak serum concentrations of azithromycin by roughly 24%.
recommendation: Take azithromycin at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after antacids.
